thread:
alex: :rotating_light: Seeing sudden 429/5xx spike for a handful of customers in US-EAST. Traffic from edge shows header-related rejects. Root deploy was a WAF/rate-limit change around 00:01 UTC.

maya: Which rule? I can roll back if it's the new RL-397 bundle.

alex: RL-397 yes. Deployed by sam via console at 00:01. Rolling back now to previous RL-396 to contain.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-279 by alex — preliminary triage in #incidents.

sam: rolled back RL-397 at 00:06 UTC. Confirmed 429 rates falling from affected customers. :thumbsup:

jordan: Logs show a lot of requests with X-Customer-ID containing percent-encoded spaces and special chars. WAF RL-397 had a header regex blocking non-alphanum. Example: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-09-12T00:04:42Z src=198.51.100.23 method=POST path=/api/generate status=429 hdrs={"X-Customer-ID":"team%20alpha"} rule=RL-397
```

maya: Oh — header normalization difference between CloudFront and edge. We normalized incoming headers earlier in the stack, so valid IDs get encoded and then matched by RL-397. Bad false positive.

alex: Confirmed customer impact: 3 paying customers saw request failures. Filing customer comms draft.

security-bot: Audit log: RBAC change — "waf-rule-deploy" executed by sam (eng) at 00:01 UTC. Action: deploy_rule(bundle=RL-397).

sam: I created RL-397 off the suggested security pattern but missed the header-encoding edge case in the test set. My bad.

jordan: Immediate mitigation: rollback (done), add a temporary exception for header X-Customer-ID for known customers, and add enhanced logging to capture raw headers for 24h.

maya: Added quick exception list to edge config for known-customer-ids. Pushed logging flag: edge.logging.header_raw=on for 24h.

alex: Customer comms: short note drafted — apology, impact, mitigation, ETA for postmortem. Liaising with Account to send to affected customers after triage.

sam: For post-incident: propose these action items:
- tighten RBAC so deploy_rule requires security approval for WAF bundles targeting header rules
- add automated test for header encoding/normalization in integration suite
- record rule deployments in immutable audit log (signed) and store signing metadata in KMS
- add canary rollout for new WAF bundles (5% traffic)

jordan: +1. Also we should reject deploys that include header regexes without explicit normalization tests.

maya: Implementation notes:
```
# example guard in deploy pipeline
if rule.contains_header_regex and not rule.tests.include('header-normalization'):
    fail('missing header-normalization test')
```

security-bot: Proposed KMS flow: sign WAF bundles with customers' and platform keys. Store signature metadata in audit-log stream (BigQuery). On edge, verify signature before applying.

alex: Good. Timeline? We need quick wins first: RBAC change + require review + add normalization test. KMS signing can be medium-term (2-3 sprints).

sam: I'll open an RFC and a PR for RBAC change today. Assigning to security for review.

jordan: I'll add the header-normalization tests to the integration harness and wire a canary flag for bundle rollout.

maya: Ops: leave RL-396 as default and keep exception list until tests pass. We'll rotate exception list hourly and monitor.

incidents-bot: Status update: contained — rollback complete, exceptions applied, logging enabled. Next update in 2h or on new findings.

alex: Postmortem owner: sam. Draft due EOD tomorrow. Include customer impact timeline and action list (RBAC, tests, KMS RFC).

sam: ACK. I'll include deploy audit export and link to logs.

jordan: After-action checklist addition: add a small runbook for header-encoding issues and a playbook for WAF rule rollbacks.

maya: Noted. Also will add a console guard that shows "This rule will block encoded headers" warning if header regex present.

alex: Thanks everyone. No further customer escalations so far. Keeping this thread for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
